title: INCLUDE Study – Inclusion and Equity in Acute Care / PROM Validation; Autonomy and safety in acute care of older adults - validation of the german version of the "patient-reported outcome measure for Older Patients receiving Acute Care" (PROM-OPAC)
summary: Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) allow the patient perspective to be incorporated into the assessment and quality measurement of medical care. PROM-OPAC is a questionnaire that enables patients to report their experiences during treatment in an emergency department. It was developed for older, frail individuals receiving emergency or acute care. The questionnaire assesses how safe and autonomous patients feel during their treatment. In this study, a German version will be created and first tested for comprehensibility, followed by an evaluation of its reliability in measuring the intended outcomes.
conditions: Cultural adaptation and validation of PROM-OPAC

interventions.name:
Emergency department patients aged 70 years and older
Study Phase 1: Conducting cognitive interviews for the cultural validation of the German-language version of PROM-OPAC following emergency care and the development of the finalized German-language version G-PROM-OPAC

Study Phase 2: Validation

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
German as a native language or proficiency in German at a near-native level (at least C1).
Exclusion criteria:
Medical reasons precluding participation (e.g., mechanical ventilation, resuscitation in the emergency room), insufficient proficiency in the survey language, lack of capacity to provide informed consent, or the presence of legal guardianship.
